```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Test of the MPFF Word template with officedown
# ==============================================================================
# Build with build_report.R (fills in the cover page and footers first).
# What to check in the result:
#   - cover page and version history from MPFF_report_front.docx
#   - table of contents, unnumbered and numbered headings in the MPFF styles
#   - figure and table captions numbered by Word, with cross-references
#   - a landscape page
# ==============================================================================

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, dpi = 200)

library(officedown)
library(officer)
library(flextable)
library(ggplot2)

# Example data
landings_example <- data.frame(
  year    = rep(2015:2023, 3),
  country = rep(c("FRA", "NLD", "GBR"), each = 9),
  tonnes  = c(seq(40, 32, length.out = 9), seq(12, 10, length.out = 9), seq(20, 15, length.out = 9)) * 1000
)
```

```{r front-page}
# Cover page, citation and version history (filled in by build_report.R)
block_pour_docx("word_build/MPFF_report_front_filled.docx")
```

Executive summary

This paragraph is in the template's Normal style. Headings below are numbered by the template; this heading uses the unnumbered style "Hheading 1".

Total landings in the example data were `r format(round(sum(landings_example$tonnes)), big.mark = ",")` t. Inline numbers like this one are calculated when the report is knitted.

# Introduction {#intro}

# Material & Methods {#methods}

Figure \@ref(fig:landings-plot) shows the example landings, and Table \@ref(tab:landings-table) gives the same numbers as a table.

# Results

## Landings {#results-landings}

```{r landings-plot, fig.cap="Landings (t) per year by country (example data)."}
ggplot(landings_example, aes(x = year, y = tonnes / 1000, colour = country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Landings (1000 t)", colour = "Country") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r landings-table, tab.id="landings-table", tab.cap="Landings (t) per year by country (example data)."}
landings_wide <- tidyr::pivot_wider(landings_example, names_from = country, values_from = tonnes)

flextable(landings_wide) |>
  colformat_num(j = -1, big.mark = ",", digits = 0) |>
  colformat_num(j = 1, big.mark = "", digits = 0) |>
  font(fontname = "Calibri", part = "all") |>
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
  bold(part = "header") |>
  autofit()
```

## A landscape page

Wide tables or figures can be placed on a landscape page like this one.

```{r wide-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="The same figure on a landscape page."}
ggplot(landings_example, aes(x = year, y = tonnes / 1000, fill = country)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~country) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Landings (1000 t)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
